text:
cheng: quick heads-up, perf probe from this morning (stress run on h100/a100 clusters) shows odd kernel pick shifts for quantized flavors. short seqs (<64) are getting INT8 kernels on h100 (good), but midseq (128-512) on a100 are flipping to INT4 and we see 20-40ms tail spikes and occasional OOM-like mem pressure. FP8 fallbacks happened in 3 traces when kv-cache warmed late.

alex: can you paste the probe trace id?

cheng: trace: https://telemetry.redwood/probes/rv-2026-03-17-19 — summary attached in logs:
```
# sample
arch: a100
seq: 256
pick: int4_kernel_v3
latency_p95: 412ms (+34ms)
kv_warmup_hits: 0/4
mem_spike: +120MB
```

maria: interesting — autotuner hysteresis thresholds look too low for a100 midseq. might be aggressively preferring int4 for cost but not accounting for KV chunking overhead.

jt: batching heuristics also changed yesterday (batch_kick_threshold lowered from 16->12). could be increasing head-of-line variance so kv cache warming is delayed.

alex: suggestion: increase per-arch longseq penalty for int4 on a100, add kv_warmup grace window for picks, and raise batch_kick_threshold back to 16. small config snippet: 
```
autotuner:
  per_arch:
    a100:
      int4_penalty: 1.15
      kv_warmup_tokens: 48
    h100:
      int4_penalty: 0.95
  batch_kick_threshold: 16
  pick_hysteresis_ms: 40
```

cheng: thanks. also saw cold-path picks where int8 was faster for short seq on h100 but runtime still chose int4 because cost model predicted token savings — mismatch in throughput probe. need to capture actual kernel throughput telemetry per-slot (tokens/sec) rather than just cost estimate.

maria: I can run a focused bench to produce per-kernel throughput profiles and a slot-level kv-warmup heatmap. will run on canary nodes (rv-canary-3).

jt: small experimental idea — add transient fallback rule: if kv_warmup_hits < 2 within first 3 steps, prefer kernels with smaller startup overhead (even if cost higher). reduces tail spikes. pseudocode: 
```
if kv_hits_firstN < 2 and seq>64:
  prefer startup_light_kernels
```

alex: also add metric: `quant_kernel_mismatch` — increments when chosen kernel differs from empirically fastest kernel for that arch/seq bucket. roll this into alerting if >0.5% for 10m.

ops-bot: deploy queued: config/pr-3945 to canary cluster (rv-canary-3). deploy id: dpl-2026-03-17-88

cheng: running the bench now. can we tag the probe with `coverage:kv,coverage:throughput` so Optimize picks it up?

maria: yep tagging. will share CSV and pickled pprof. expect results in ~45m.

alex: if bench confirms, plan: (1) bump a100 int4_penalty and kv_warmup_tokens, (2) revert batch_kick_threshold, (3) add transient fallback rule, (4) add `quant_kernel_mismatch` metric and dashboard. 

jt: ack. I can land the transient fallback in a small patch — should be low-risk.

cheng: thanks team :thumbsup: let's reconvene after maria posts bench. if anyone sees high error rates in canary abort the deploy (ops-bot will auto-rollback on error>0.5%).

maria: uploading initial CSV now — https://telemetry.redwood/uploads/rv-canary-3/kv-throughput-2026-03-17.csv

cheng: got it. first glance: a100 int4 pick improves token-cost by 12% but increases P95 by 10-15% for seq 128-384. I'll attach a short trace sample to the probe.

alex: make sure to include per-kernel memory high-water mark in report, that was where we saw the 120MB bump.

cheng: added mem HWM. will follow up with a small PR for default per-arch knobs if bench confirms.

ops-bot: deploy succeeded: dpl-2026-03-17-88 -> rv-canary-3 (ok)
